name: Frances Mendez
home: the streets inland from Pier Beach
life: “I still remember ordering soup from a mother who couldn't lift a full pan.” On Wednesday, near the market by Market Flats, Frances often waits until the delivery baskets are stacked before going in.
voice: My mother orders one small lunch. We can't pay a delivery charge five times a week and she can't store five meals.
appearance: Frances has a round face with a pronounced chin. Look for brown hair pinned away from the temples. On an ordinary day, the familiar outfit is a soft blue checked shirt with a thin silver ring worn on a cord. In conversation Frances turns fully toward the person speaking.
personality: Frances treats a small promise with the gravity others reserve for a contract. This makes Frances lovely to rely on and surprisingly difficult to invite on a whim.
agenda: To keep the mother's lunches affordable and fresh.
family: Emma Carbone is Frances’s stepsibling. Frances is free to hang up first. Emma makes the call. Some of their best calls last less than a minute. A change of tone is sometimes all the news either one needs. Asked about *Level with the window*, Emma says, “I wanted to photograph the window from the bus.”
connections: Jasper Baker. Three neighbors' lunch rounds can keep the mother's meals fresh enough to eat.

reactions.situation: A housebound customer cannot afford the delivery fee
reactions.response: Frances asks whether combining a delivery with a willing neighbor would help.

reactions.situation: A witness is embarrassed about remembering only a little
reactions.response: Frances writes down their exact words with room left for uncertainty and gives them back to check.
